cases.expected: Changes public Convex functions in place: listItems becomes paginated and searchItems drops article bodies, so every installed build breaks against the new backend (or the new bundle against the old one). Needs expand/contract.
The quiet re-classify after a note edit writes the model's new title over the note's existing title, so a note is renamed after every burst of typing: an AI pass overwriting user content.
The refund-data consent is a blocking screen after onboarding, so every new iOS account sees an 'Updated terms' wall right after the paywall, for an optional opt-in whose decline equals the default.

similarItems' full-text fallback drops words under 4 characters, so older saves sharing only a short tag (art, diy, ux) are never found; the recall card says 'N earlier saves' for every match while showing at most 3.

The exit offer sheet hosts RevenueCat's paywall full-screen with no close of its own; when the design fails to render, RevenueCat's fallback has no close either, so the user is stuck until they buy or the offer ends.

A page over the 1 MiB fetch cap arrives truncated, but the truncation is not surfaced, so recipe extraction can read a full ingredient list plus a method cut short and save it as a complete recipe that replaces the article.

pin.it resolution reads the landing page with a 64 KiB cap and stalls draining the rest until the 15 s deadline, so every pin.it link times out; a deleted pin redirects to Pinterest home with 200 and saves as a blank 'Pinterest' item.

The widget sync guards its query with TanStack's `enabled`, which the Convex adapter ignores; with a 24 h gcTime the subscription outlives unmount and sign-out and keeps being re-evaluated with no identity.

registerDevice re-binds an enabled push token row owned by another account (pushes go to the wrong user); client time zones are not validated, so one bad row makes digest preparation throw; due digests are not paginated.
After Android process death the restored task replays the last share intent on cold start, and the share screen asks 'Save it again?' every launch for a batch that was already saved.

A paywall that never shows at the end of onboarding (RevenueCat not ready, offline) is counted as a decline: the practice share is dropped and starter spaces wait; a relaunch on the reminder step skips the reminder.
The onboarding demo saves through the real share sheet but never records the first-share flag, so demo completers land on Home and are shown how to share seconds after doing it.
